Cornell frat house rape accuser 'under siege' online, says lawyer
- Published
The lawyer for the woman who alleges she was raped at a Cornell University fraternity house says she is "not doing well" as she finds herself "under siege" from online sleuths seeking to identity her.

Thomas Giuffra said the woman known in legal documents as Jane Doe was "incapable of consent" because she was "completely, grossly intoxicated" when she turned up at the home where she says the assault took place.
The woman alleges she was assaulted by seven men at the campus in Ithaca, New York, in 2024.

articles.title_original: Hawaii's iconic 550-year-old Hōlei Sea Arch collapses
articles.title_zh: Hawaii's iconic 550-year-old Hōlei Sea Arch collapses
facts_zh:
Hawaii's iconic 550-year-old Hōlei Sea Arch collapses
- Published
Hawaii's famous Hōlei Sea Arch, a 90-foot-tall (27.4m) lava rock structure that formed about 550 years ago, has collapsed into the Pacific Ocean.
The collapse's exact time is not known.
The arch was still projecting into the water from the coast of Volcanoes National Park on 23 September, but was gone by 27 September, the National Park Service (NPS) said.

articles.title_zh: US murderer Christa Pike unconscious and on ventilator after failed execution, lawyers say
facts_zh:
US murderer Christa Pike unconscious and on ventilator after failed execution, lawyers say
- Published
Warning: This article contains details that readers may find distressing
Tennessee death row inmate Christa Pike was unconscious, intubated and on a ventilator on Thursday night, after authorities failed to execute her by lethal injection, her lawyers say in court filings.
Pike, 50, was injected with two lethal doses of pentobarbital on Wednesday but remained alive.
She was then sent to hospital in an ambulance.

facts_zh:
G7 to release 100 million barrels of oil and diesel after Trump export ban threat
- Published
The G7 has agreed to release 100 million barrels of oil and diesel in a bid to ease supply pressures that have caused prices to skyrocket.
The group of advanced economies, including the US, said the move would include a "substantial release" of diesel in the coming days.
President Donald Trump had threatened to ban diesel exports in a move which would have eased pressure on prices for US consumers ahead of November's midterm elections, but pushed up prices elsewhere.

Riot police have clashed with protesters as thousands of students demonstrating over education standards disrupted more than 560 schools in France on Friday.
Fires have burned in the streets as high school pupils and others objected to a lack of teachers, overcrowded classrooms and run-down buildings.
The protests began last week in Paris and have spread across the country, with cities including Montpellier, Nantes and Marseille affected.

articles.title_zh: Ethiopia and Eritrea cut diplomatic ties as northern conflict escalates
facts_zh:
Ethiopia and Eritrea cut diplomatic ties as northern conflict escalates
- Published
Ethiopia and Eritrea have severed diplomatic relations as renewed fighting in northern Ethiopia raises fears of a wider regional conflict.

On Thursday, Ethiopia announced it was closing its embassy in the Eritrean capital, Asmara, and ordered 10 Eritrean diplomats to leave the country within 48 hours, accusing them of activities that threatened national security.
Eritrea responded by cutting diplomatic relations, saying Ethiopia's decision had left it with no choice but to take reciprocal action.

all_titles.en: Ethiopia and Eritrea cut diplomatic ties as northern conflict escalates

articles.title_zh: Spanish PM Sánchez loses key housing crisis vote after eviction of woman, 87
facts_zh:
Spanish PM Sánchez loses key housing crisis vote after eviction of woman, 87
- Published
Spain's Congress has rejected a series of measures aimed at tackling the country's housing crisis, in a defeat for the government of Pedro Sánchez that increases pressure on him to call a snap election.
Lawmakers voted on two decree-laws presented by the government in response to nationwide protests that have followed the eviction of an 87-year-old woman, Maricarmen Abascal, from her home.
The decrees, which introduced a series of initiatives aimed at protecting tenants in the rental market, required parliamentary approval in order to remain in place.

Intensified Russian drone and missile strikes are "tearing Kyiv apart", the mayor of Ukraine's capital has warned.

He was speaking after Kyiv's defence council held a crisis meeting, following new Russian strikes on a key bridge that caused traffic chaos.

articles.title_zh: I've seen nearly 500 executions - but never one like Christa Pike's
facts_zh:
I've seen nearly 500 executions - but never one like Christa Pike's
- Published
Reporter Michael Graczyk has covered nearly 500 executions carried out in Texas, continuing even after his 2018 retirement from The Associated Press.
He remembers two instances where needles popped out before reinsertion for successful execution - but never one in which an inmate survived.

That's what happened this week in Tennessee, when 50-year-old inmate Christa Pike remained breathing and audibly snoring after two separate doses of pentobarbital, the barbiturate used in the state's lethal injection protocol.

all_titles.en: I've seen nearly 500 executions - but never one like Christa Pike's

articles.title_original: Cornell students gather to voice anger over alleged gang rape
articles.title_zh: Cornell students gather to voice anger over alleged gang rape
facts_zh:
'Ashamed': Cornell students gather to voice anger over alleged gang rape
- Published
Students have called for drastic change at Cornell University as a result of an alleged gang rape in 2024, with one using an emotional student assembly on Thursday to say: "We're absolutely ashamed of the events that happened on campus."
Students and faculty members say the investigation into the incident has cast a "dark cloud" over the campus - stirring anger, concern over fraternity culture, and a backlash against the university's handling of the situation.
At Thursday's assembly, some labelled the perceived lack of justice a "disgrace" and criticised the prestigious university, which has defended its handling of the case.
"We deserve to know that our institution values our safety more than its reputation," undergraduate Sophia Riley Sim told those at the gathering.

all_titles.en: Cornell students gather to voice anger over alleged gang rape

articles.title_original: 'I was not going to let others die' - pilot of Flydubai flight describes cockpit attack by co-pilot
articles.title_zh: 'I was not going to let others die' - pilot of Flydubai flight describes cockpit attack by co-pilot
facts_zh:
'I was not going to let others die' - pilot of Flydubai flight describes cockpit attack by co-pilot
- Published
The Indian pilot of the Flydubai plane who was stabbed by his co-pilot and opened the cockpit door to let others in has said he was determined not to let others die.
Capt Smit Machchhar said he was on the floor and still being attacked when he realised the plane carrying more than 170 passengers was sinking and he had to do something.
"I was lying on the floor injured but I told myself to go for one last push to open the door from inside," he said in a video call with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

all_titles.en: 'I was not going to let others die' - pilot of Flydubai flight describes cockpit attack by co-pilot

OpenAI fires workers for 'mishandling sensitive information'
- Published
OpenAI has fired three researchers for allegedly mishandling information, including work which involved an external organisation analysing AI models.

"Our investigation confirmed that these individuals mishandled sensitive information outside established company procedures, violating our policies and breaking the trust essential to our work," a spokesperson told the BBC.
The ChatGPT-maker did not name the sacked workers, but at least two of them were involved in safety research at the firm.

facts_zh:
Japan's first mayor to take maternity leave lands on TIME100 Next list
- Published
Shoko Kawata, Japan's first mayor to take maternity leave, has been named one of the 100 most influential rising stars by TIME Magazine.
The recognition comes weeks after the 36-year-old gave birth to her first child on 15 September.
Earlier this year, Kawata, who is mayor of Yawata City in Kyoto prefecture, was plunged into a national debate about whether elected officials should take time off for childbirth.
